info.title: Provision LLM Engine API
info.description:
OpenAI-compatible + native endpoints exposed by the Provision LLM Engine (llama-server). Served by the server itself, so "Try it out" runs same-origin (no CORS setup needed). In router mode, send a known model id in the `model` field (e.g. `qwen2.5-chat`, `gte-qwen2-embed`).

**Licensed builds** (image `:release`): endpoints tagged _counted_ are metered by the license subsystem. A request is charged one unit per result it produces (a `prompt` / `input` / `documents` array or `n` > 1 counts per element) and only when a 2xx result is delivered; errors and requests the client abandons are not charged. The trial allows 50 requests per install; after that, or with no / an expired license, counted endpoints return HTTP 403 with an `error.license` block and `X-License-Mode` / `X-License-Used` / `X-License-Limit` headers until the product is activated via `POST /license/activate`. Endpoints tagged _exempt_ (health, metadata, tokenize, models, slots, `/license/*`) never consume the budget. Unlicensed builds (`:dev`) have no counter and answer 404 on `/license/*`.

Many routes have aliases (legacy / non-`v1` forms); the canonical path is documented and its aliases are listed in the route description.

**Admin API** (`/admin/*`, tag _Admin_): present only when the server runs in router mode with `PROVISION_ADMIN=1` (otherwise these paths answer 404). In the Docker deployment, and with the host nginx site of `deploy/linux/`, the nginx front door forwards `/admin` (and `/cors-proxy`) only for allow-listed client addresses and answers 403 to everyone else. Every endpoint except the `GET /admin/status` probe also needs the admin key in the `X-Admin-Key` header (use **Authorize**). Loading, unloading, downloading and deleting downloaded models keep using the public model routes (`/models`, `/models/load`, `/models/unload`); the settings, the upload of GGUF files (`/admin/models/upload*`) and the deletion of models of the models directory (`/admin/models/delete`) are protected by the admin key. Admin endpoints never consume the license budget.

get.description: Effective settings plus what the settings form needs: limits, the devices mentioned by the model presets, the GPUs of this server (`build_devices`) and the model list with the pinned flag. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.description:
Send any subset of the three settings; fields that are left out keep their value. The request is validated as a whole: on any error nothing is saved. On success the settings are stored in the admin state directory, applied immediately and returned.

- `models_max`: applies to every later scheduling decision. Raising it takes effect at once; lowering it does not unload anything by itself.
- `pinned`: a pinned model is never unloaded to make room for another one. At least one slot must stay free: `pinned` must be shorter than `models_max`.
- `default_device`: GPU for models that have no `device` of their own (downloaded or dropped-in models; sections of `models.ini` are not touched by it, they get a GPU of their own through `POST /admin/models/settings`). A name this server does not have is not applied (`warnings`: `default_device_not_present`). Changing it rebuilds the model list, which unloads a **running** model whose arguments changed. Rejected with 409 while `MODEL_DEVICES` contains a `*=` entry.

**Exempt** from the trial budget.

400.description: Validation failed, nothing was saved (`error.type` = `invalid_request_error`): `models_max` outside `limits`, malformed `default_device`, unknown model id in `pinned`, or `pinned` not shorter than `models_max`

get.description: The directories the server keeps models and admin state in, with the free space of the filesystem each one lives on, and unfinished downloads found in the model cache. The `models_dir` entry is absent when the server runs without `--models-dir`. `uploads` lists the unfinished GGUF uploads (`/admin/models/upload`) with what they take on disk, `upload_staging` their folder and the trash of deleted models; this call also runs the clean-up of that folder. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.summary: Pre-flight check for a model download (exempt)
post.description: Advisory only: asks the configured Hugging Face endpoint which files `POST /models` would fetch for this model, adds up their size and compares it with the free space of the model cache. It downloads nothing and never blocks a download; problems are reported as codes in `warnings`. The answer is always 200 for a well-formed request, also when Hugging Face cannot be reached (network budget: about 10 s). The download itself is started with the public `POST /models {"model": ...}`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

get.summary: Per-model settings of all models, or of one (exempt)
get.description: Without `model`: every model of the list with its custom settings (`overrides`), the effective value and origin of every whitelisted key (`fields`), locks, the trial / commit state and the last failure, plus the saved settings of models that are no longer in the list (`unattached`) and the state of `admin-models.json`. Model facts are included when they are already known (they are read in the background). With `?model=<id>`: that one row (plus `state`), with the facts read from its file if needed; for an id that is only in `unattached`, its saved entry (`exists: false`). **Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.summary: Change one model's settings, optionally restart it (exempt)
post.description:
Sets custom settings of one model (a value) or removes them (`null`); keys that are not given stay as they are. `reset: true` removes all custom settings of the model (also for an entry in `unattached`). Only the whitelisted keys of `AdminModelSettingsInput` are accepted; `cache-type-k` and `cache-type-v` must be equal; a quantized KV cache needs flash attention other than `off`. A value equal to the built-in default with nothing inherited counts as "not set", so it never changes anything.

- Model **running** and the change needs a restart: refused with 409 `restart_required` unless `restart: true`; nothing is saved. With `restart: true` the model is stopped first (at most its stop timeout + 10 s, else 504 `stop_timeout` and nothing is saved), then the settings are saved, the model list is rebuilt (like a rescan: models that were loaded and are down afterwards are loaded again, `restarted_also` / `not_restarted`) and the model is started again.
- Model **not running**: saved; with `restart: true` also loaded right away ("Save and load").
- New settings are first tried (`phase` `trial`); after two failed starts in a row the server goes back to the last settings that worked (`reverted`).

The POST holds the request until the restart has begun (up to the stop timeout + 10 s); follow the load on `GET /models/sse`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.summary: Will these settings fit? Dry run by llama.cpp (exempt)
post.description: Runs a short helper process of the server binary with the arguments the model would get with these (unsaved) settings. It uses llama.cpp's own fit machinery: the model and its context are built without allocating the weights, and the need per GPU (model, context, compute) and on the host is reported. The verdict per GPU compares the need plus a 1 GiB margin with the memory `available` there (free now, from the vendor tool or the helper, plus the model's own use if it is running and would be restarted); `verdict` is the worst of them. A model that uses no GPU (a CPU-only server, or `device` `none`) gets the verdict `cpu_only`. One check at a time (409 `check_busy`; 409 `check_stuck` while a stopped helper has not exited), at most 30 s. A result is reused (`cached`) for at most 60 s, while the model's effective arguments, the GPU inventory and the model's state (running or not) are unchanged and the live free memory of its GPUs moved by less than 256 MiB: llama.cpp's fit adapts the values left on auto to the memory free at that moment. `checked_while_running` marks a dry run made while the model was running (its fit saw the model's own memory as used). Nothing is saved. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

200.description: Result of the check; `ok: false` with `error` when llama.cpp could not set the model up

get.description: Every GPU of the server with total / used / free memory and the models placed on it. GPUs come from the inventory the server takes at start-up (and on `POST /admin/gpus/rescan`) in a helper process: names, backend, PCI bus id, memory. Live memory comes from the vendor tool of each GPU vendor found (`nvidia-smi`, `amd-smi` or `rocm-smi`, see `PROVISION_ADMIN_GPU_PROBE`), matched to the GPUs by PCI bus id; without one the inventory values are shown with their age. The router itself creates no GPU context. In `auto` mode `amd-smi` / `rocm-smi` are also looked for in `$ROCM_PATH/bin` and `/opt/rocm/bin`. One vendor-tool run at a time, at most 15 s each; a request waits for it at most 5 s (then `timeout`; the late answer is used by the next request), and a tool still running after its 15 s is reported as `probe_stuck`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

Every item has a status (`ok`, `warning`, `error`, `info`) and a one-line hint. While a fit check or inventory helper hangs (stopped, not exited), an item `stuck_helpers` (status `error`) is added at the end. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

get.summary: Uploads: availability, limits and the uploads of this server, or one upload (exempt)
get.description:
Without `id`: whether GGUF files can be uploaded on this server (`available`; else `reason`: `no_models_dir`, `models_dir_missing`, `not_writable`, `staging_unusable`, `staging_other_filesystem`, and `message`), the fixed `limits`, every upload of this server (from every browser and admin, finished ones for 24 h, so a client that lost its files can offer to continue), `staging_bytes`, and whether the placement of an upload can be saved (`settings_writable`).

With `?id=<upload id>`: one upload with everything a client needs to continue it. Per file: `offset` (the bytes the server accepted; the next chunk starts here), `durable_offset` (on disk at the last checkpoint; after a restart of the server `offset` goes back to it), `complete`, `dropped`, `role`, `sha256`, `head_crc32` (CRC-32 of the first MiB, to compare with a file picked again), `final_name`, `header` (the header check of that file) and `error` (why the file cannot be used). The upload: `state` `receiving`, `checking` (`substate` `queued`, `hashing` with `progress`, `classifying`, `load_check`), `ready` (`blocked_by` `manual`, `name_taken`, `publish_error`, `check_failed`, `sha256_mismatch`, `settings_not_saved`, `settings_invalid`; details in `blocked`), `publishing`, `published` (`result`), `rejected` (`error`), `cancelled`, `expired`; plus `checks`, `plan`, `facts`, `warnings`, `last_activity`, `expires_at` (72 h without progress, counted while the server runs), `idle_ms` and `last_client_idle_ms`.

The upload routes never answer 404 for an upload (the server replaces the body of every 404); an unknown or removed upload is 410 `upload_gone`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.
get.x-s3-recheck: aligned with tools/server/server-admin-upload.cpp while it was being written: re-check every field, and the shapes of plan / facts / result

post.summary: Create the upload of one model, or check it (dry run) (exempt)
post.description:
One upload is one model: a single GGUF file, or a complete split set, plus at most one projector (`mmproj`). Draft models are not supported (400 `unsupported_file`).

- `name` becomes the model id: `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`; refused without regard to case: containing `mmproj` or `.gguf`, starting with `mtp-` / `dspark-` / `dflash-` / `eagle3-`, containing `-NNNNN-of-NNNNN`, ending in `.`, Windows reserved names (400 `invalid_name` with `reason`). It must be unique, without regard to case, among the ids and aliases of the model list, the entries of the models directory as the scanner names them, and the other unfinished uploads (409 `name_taken` with `by`); checked again at update and right before publishing.
- `files`: 1 to 256, each at least 24 bytes; `name` is only shown and used for matching after a reload, never as a path; an optional `sha256` (64 hex characters) is compared after the last byte (a mismatch makes the upload wait as `ready` / `sha256_mismatch`).
- `settings`: per-model settings (as `POST /admin/models/settings`, including the lock rules: 409 `field_locked`), saved as the model's per-model settings right before its files become visible, so its first start uses them. `settings_mode` `replace` (default) drops saved settings of an earlier model with this id, `keep` uses them again (`existing_settings` shows them).
- `auto_publish` (default true): publish as soon as the checks pass.
- `dry_run`: check only, nothing is created (200, `upload.id` null).

`warnings` never block (disk space is warn-only): `not_enough_space`, `larger_than_disk`, `shares_disk_with_state`, `record_not_persisted`. The files are then sent with `POST /admin/models/upload/chunk`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.
post.x-s3-recheck: the create answer (upload = the full upload view; existing_settings only when present; the shape of locks) and the by values of name_taken

post.summary: Append one chunk of a file of an upload (exempt)
post.description:
The body is the raw bytes `offset .. offset + length - 1` of file `file` (at most `chunk_max`, 16 MiB; `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`; a `Content-Length` is required, no chunked transfer encoding). The server handles a chunk only once it has the whole body, so its offset moves by whole chunks only and sending a chunk again is always safe:

- `offset` equal to the server's offset: appended.
- `offset` before it: the part the server already has is compared byte for byte with what it stored (409 `content_mismatch` when it differs: not the same file); the rest is appended. Sending the first MiB and up to 1 MiB before the offset after a reload proves that a file picked again is the same.
- `offset` after it: 409 `offset_mismatch` with the server's `offset`.

`X-Upload-Client` names the sender (a random id per browser tab, kept for the tab session); a chunk from another sender within 30 s of the last one is 409 `other_client_active` unless `takeover=1`. `X-Chunk-CRC32` (optional) is checked before the bytes are stored (400 `crc_mismatch`). The first chunk of a file shows whether it is GGUF (422 `not_gguf`) and starts the header check; a file it finds unusable gets 422 `file_rejected` (only that file: drop it with `update` or cancel), a model it cannot accept rejects the upload within seconds (unsupported architecture, projector as the model, inconsistent split set).

Answered before the body is read: no or a wrong key, an address the allow-list refuses, no `Content-Length` (411), a `Content-Length` above `chunk_max` (413 `chunk_too_large`, JSON; a 413 without this JSON comes from a proxy: send smaller chunks), an upload that is busy or over, another sender, a chunk of this upload already on its way (409 `chunk_in_progress`), too many chunks at once (429 `upload_slots_busy`). Every answer of 400 or above closes the connection; a client that is still sending may see a reset connection and then asks `GET /admin/models/upload?id=` where to continue. Also expect upstream's 503 while the server starts and 401 from `--api-key`. **Exempt** from the trial budget.
post.x-s3-recheck: the early-refusal set of the pre-body hook (spec B.5c) and the 422 file_rejected path

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: `index` of the file in the upload

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Byte offset of the first byte of the body in the file

parameters.name: takeover
parameters.description: `1` = make this sender the one that writes, although another one wrote within the last 30 s

parameters.name: X-Upload-Client
parameters.description: Random id of the sending browser tab or script

parameters.name: X-Chunk-CRC32
parameters.description: CRC-32 (IEEE, as in zip and gzip) of the body, 8 hexadecimal digits

200.description: Stored (or compared, when the whole chunk was already there)

400.description: `invalid_request_error` (`param`: `id`, `file`, `offset`, `X-Chunk-CRC32`), `beyond_declared_size` (the chunk reaches beyond the declared size of the file), `crc_mismatch` (`X-Chunk-CRC32` does not match the body)

409.description: `offset_mismatch` (`offset`: where the server is), `content_mismatch` (the bytes sent again differ: not the same file), `chunk_in_progress` (another chunk of this upload is on its way), `other_client_active` (`idle_ms`; another sender wrote within 30 s: send `takeover=1`), `upload_busy` (`state`: the upload is being checked or published, or waits as ready), `file_dropped` (the file was dropped from the upload)

error.message: this file has 8388608 bytes so far: continue at that offset

411.description: `length_required`: the chunk has no `Content-Length` (chunked transfer encoding is not accepted)

413.description: `chunk_too_large` (`chunk_max`): the body is larger than `chunk_max`. Only this JSON answer comes from the server; a 413 without it comes from a proxy in front of it

error.message: a chunk may hold at most 16777216 bytes

422.description: `not_gguf` (`file`): the file does not start with `GGUF` and version 2 or 3; `file_rejected` (`file`, `code`): the check found the file unusable. Only that file is affected; the rest of the upload stays

500.description: `write_failed`: an error while writing other than a full disk; the chunk is discarded, the upload is kept

507.description: `disk_full` (`free_bytes`, `offset`, `durable_offset`): the disk is full or a quota is reached; the chunk is discarded, the upload is kept. Free space, then continue from `offset`

error.message: the disk is full: free space, then resume the upload (or cancel it to free its space)

post.summary: Change an upload: name, settings, expected SHA-256, drop files (exempt)
post.description: Only while the upload is `receiving` or `ready`. A new `name` is checked as at create (409 `name_taken`); nothing is uploaded again, which is how an upload waiting as `ready` / `name_taken` is renamed. `settings` replaces the settings of the upload; `settings_mode` and `auto_publish` as at create. `files` sets (or with an empty string removes) the expected SHA-256 of files by `index`; `drop_files` takes files out of the upload (for example one that is not GGUF) and deletes their data at once; when the files that are left are all complete the checks start. 409 `upload_busy` while it is being checked or published, 410 once it is over. **Exempt** from the trial budget.
post.x-s3-recheck: files[] / drop_files and the answer shape

sha.summary: Correct the expected SHA-256 of file 0

post.summary: Publish an upload that waits as ready, or run its checks again (exempt)
post.description: For an upload in `ready`: `manual` (auto_publish off), after a rename (`name_taken`), after a `publish_error`. For `check_failed` and `sha256_mismatch` the checks run again; `ignore_sha256_mismatch: true` accepts a SHA-256 that differs from the expected one (publish anyway). `without_settings: true` publishes without the upload's settings (`settings_not_saved`; the model then starts with its inherited values). Publishing: the name is checked again, the settings are saved as the model's per-model settings, the files become visible with one rename that never replaces anything, and the model list is rebuilt; the model then appears not loaded. Answers 202 at once (`publishing` or `checking`): follow it with `GET /admin/models/upload?id=`. An upload that is already published answers 200; one that is publishing or checking answers with its state. **Exempt** from the trial budget.
post.x-s3-recheck: ignore_sha256_mismatch / without_settings and the answer shape

anyway.summary: Publish anyway with a differing SHA-256

post.summary: Cancel an upload and delete its data (exempt)
post.description: Ends an upload that is not published yet and deletes its data at once (`freed_bytes`). An upload that is already over answers 200 with `cancelled` false or true and `freed_bytes` 0. **Exempt** from the trial budget.

post.summary: Delete a model of the models directory, or only its projector (exempt)
post.description:
For models with source `models_dir` (uploaded or dropped in by hand); downloaded models keep `DELETE /models`, sections of `models.ini` are changed in `models.ini` (409 `not_deletable`). Only the files the model uses are deleted: its GGUF file or every shard of a split model, its projector and its draft model. Other entries of its folder stay (`kept`); the folder is removed only when it is empty afterwards. `projector_only` (Remove projector) deletes only the projector file; the model stays.

- `dry_run`: only report (`files`, `n_files`, `total_bytes`; `kept`, at most 100 listed; `running`, `pinned`, `has_settings`, `warnings`).
- A running model is refused (409 `model_running`) unless `stop`; then it is stopped first with a deadline of its stop timeout + 10 s (504 `stop_timeout`, nothing deleted).
- `remove_settings` (default true) also removes the model's saved per-model settings, its pin and what the server cached about it.

The files are moved into a trash folder inside the models directory first (out of the model list at once), the model list is rebuilt, and the trash is deleted in the background (`trash_left`). An unknown id is 409 `not_deletable` with `reason` `not_found` (never 404). **Exempt** from the trial budget.
post.x-s3-recheck: aligned with up_handle_delete in server-admin-upload.cpp while it was being written: re-check every field and reason

200.description: The dry run, or what was deleted

error.message: model 'gemma-3-4b' is running: send "stop": true to stop it first

500.description: `server_error`: the trash folder could not be created or the model's folder could not be opened

504.description: `stop_timeout`: the running model did not stop within its stop timeout + 10 s; nothing was deleted

AdminKey.name: X-Admin-Key
AdminKey.description: Admin key: `PROVISION_ADMIN_KEY`, the first line of `PROVISION_ADMIN_KEY_FILE`, or the key the server generated into `<admin state dir>/admin.key`

TrialLimitReached.description: Refused by the license gate (licensed builds only): the trial budget or the licence's request limit is used up, a batch does not fit into what is left, or there is no valid / an expired license. Nothing is charged for a refused request.

X-Trial-Limit.description: Trial mode only: same as X-License-Limit

X-Trial-Used.description: Trial mode only: same as X-License-Used

error.message: Trial limit reached: this evaluation build allows 50 inference requests and all of them are used. Activate a license to continue (Settings -> License in the web UI, or POST /license/activate).

AdminKeyRequired.description: The `X-Admin-Key` header is missing or wrong

error.message: a valid X-Admin-Key header is required

AdminKeyUnavailable.description: The server has no admin key: none is configured and the admin state directory is not writable, so none could be generated

AdminAddressNotAllowed.description: `admin_forbidden`: the client address is not on the `/admin` allow-list. Answered by the nginx front door (Docker: `ADMIN_ALLOW_RULES`; host: the `geo` allow-list of `deploy/linux/nginx-provision-llm.conf`), where the request never reaches the server, or by the server's own allow-list (`PROVISION_ADMIN_ALLOW_FROM`, off by default; `X-Forwarded-For` is used only from the reverse proxies in `PROVISION_ADMIN_TRUSTED_PROXIES`), whose message names the address the server saw. The server's allow-list applies to every `/admin` route, the status probe included, before the key check; while one of its entries cannot be read, every `/admin` request is refused (fail closed)

error.message: The admin API is not available from this address
The admin API is not available from this address; the server sees the request coming from 10.64.1.7

locked.summary: Server allow-list with an invalid entry

error.message: The admin API is locked: the address allow-list of the server has an invalid entry (see the server log); the request comes from 10.64.0.7

AdminDisabled.description: The admin layer is not enabled (`PROVISION_ADMIN` unset) or the server is not running in router mode

AdminUploadGone.description: `upload_gone` (`state`): the upload is unknown, expired, cancelled, rejected or published (its data is gone or published)

AdminModelNotFound.description: No model with this id and no saved settings for it (`not_found_error`). The server replaces the body of every 404 with its generic `File Not Found` answer. Also answered when the admin layer is not enabled or the server is not running in router mode

mode.description: `none` = no usable license: counted endpoints answer 403 until activation

status.description: `valid` = counted endpoints are served right now

limit.description: Request limit; -1 = unlimited licence, 0 = no license loaded

windowResetsAt.description: When the 30-day request window resets (licence with a request limit only)

activationCode.description: Code issued by the License Server

AdminStatus.description: Without a valid key only the three required fields are present

admin.description: Always true: the admin layer is enabled

key_configured.description: false = the server has no admin key (protected endpoints answer 503)

version.description: Version of the admin state format

key_source.description: Where the key comes from: `PROVISION_ADMIN_KEY`, `PROVISION_ADMIN_KEY_FILE`, or `<state dir>/admin.key`

features.description: Optional parts this server has: `model_settings` (`/admin/models/settings`), `gpus` (`/admin/gpus`), `model_log` (`/admin/models/log`), `diagnostics` (`/admin/diagnostics`), `fit_check` (`/admin/models/settings/check`), `upload` (`/admin/models/upload*`), `delete` (`/admin/models/delete`). Clients show those parts only when listed; an older server has no `features`

warnings.description: `default_device_not_present`: GPU for new models names a GPU this server does not have (it is not applied)

max.description: Effective limit of simultaneously loaded models

running.description: Models that hold a slot right now

error.description: Why the saved settings could not be read at startup (the startup defaults are used until settings are saved again); empty when fine

available.description: The binary can make HTTPS downloads and the router is not in `--offline` mode

ip_allowlist.description: The server's own `/admin` address allow-list (`PROVISION_ADMIN_ALLOW_FROM`) is on; the details are in `GET /admin/diagnostics`, item `ip_allowlist`

source.description: `preset` = section of models.ini, `cache` = downloaded, `models_dir` = file dropped into the models directory

default_device.description: GPU for models without a `device` of their own; empty = not set. While locked this is the `*=` value of `MODEL_DEVICES`

pinned_ignored.description: Configured pins that are not in effect because one slot must stay evictable

pinned_unknown.description: Configured pins that are not in the model list (yet); one among the first `models_max - 1` is protected as soon as it appears

build_devices.description: GPUs of this server's backends (empty for a CPU-only build); the device choices are made from this list

warnings.description: `default_device_not_present`: `default_device` names a GPU this server does not have, it is not applied

default_device.description: Empty string = clear, `none` = CPU only, or device names separated by `,` or `;` (each like `CUDA0`)

pinned.description: Ids from the model list; duplicates are removed; must be shorter than `models_max`. A request without `pinned` is checked against the pins in effect

total_bytes.description: Size of the filesystem the directory is on

partial_downloads.description: Unfinished download files (`*.downloadInProgress`) left in the model cache

uploads.description: Unfinished GGUF uploads (`/admin/models/upload`), each as in the list of `GET /admin/models/upload` plus `bytes`, what it takes on disk now; absent on servers without the `upload` feature

upload_staging.description: The folder of the unfinished uploads (`.provision-upload` in the models directory)

bytes.description: What the unfinished uploads take together

trash_bytes.description: Files of deleted models that still wait in the trash

model.description: Hugging Face repository with an optional quantization tag: `user/repo[:quant]`

quant.description: Quantization tag from the request; empty when none was given

exists.description: The repository exists and is readable with the server's token

already_present.description: The model is already in the model list / cache

files.description: Files the download would fetch (only `preset.ini` for a preset repository)

free_bytes.description: Free space of the filesystem that holds the model cache

enough_space.description: `total_bytes <= free_bytes` (no reserve is kept; a warning only)

warnings.description: `repo_not_found` also covers gated / private repositories the server has no access to. `preset_repository`: the repository holds a preset (`preset.ini`), only that file is downloaded and no model appears in the list; `no_gguf_for_quant` and `quant_not_specified` are then not reported

AdminModelSettingsInput.description: Per-model settings (keys are the `models.ini` names). A value sets a custom setting, `null` removes it; keys that are not given stay as they are. Numbers and booleans may also be sent as strings. The same object is the `settings` of an export file (`provision-llm-model-settings`)

device.description: `none` (CPU only) or 1-4 GPU names of this server (`build_devices`) joined by `,`; compared without regard to case

ctx-size.description: KV cache pool of the model in tokens, shared by its slots

kv-unified-per-slot.description: Upper limit of one request in tokens ("per request x slots" mode: `ctx-size` = slots x this)

parallel.description: Parallel requests (slots): 1-16, or -1 = auto (4, the built-in default). 0 is refused. An explicit value also makes the KV cache one shared pool unless models.ini sets kv-unified

cache-type-k.description: Must equal `cache-type-v`; a quantized type needs `flash-attn` other than `off`. Built-in default `f16`

ubatch-size.description: Micro-batch (built-in default 512); for embedding / reranking models with mean, cls or rank pooling also the longest accepted input

AdminModelField.description: One whitelisted key of one model

effective.description: Value the model process gets (canonical spelling); null = not set anywhere, the built-in `default` applies

default.description: Built-in default, when the server knows one

origin.description: Where the effective value comes from

inherited.description: Value without the custom setting (models.ini section or `[*]`, or GPU for new models)

override.description: The custom value saved in the panel; null = none

locked.description: Set when the key cannot be changed here

active.description: A custom value is saved and applied (false: none saved, or a lock / a missing device overrides it, see `inactive_reason`)

inactive_reason.description: Why a saved custom value is not applied, e.g. `router_cli`, `model_devices`, `device_missing`

AdminFailureReason.description: Why a model process failed (null when there is nothing to report)

code.description: Classified from the last error lines of the output (the last line naming a specific cause wins). `none`: no error line, the process was stopped or killed

line.description: The output line the reason comes from

hints.description: `memory_tight`: llama.cpp's fit warned that memory is short (`failed to fit params ...`); only a hint, the load often works

AdminFailure.description: The last failed start of a model; replaced only by a later failure (a retry by a client request does not wipe it)

time_ms.description: When the failure was recorded, in milliseconds since the epoch

before_loaded.description: The process ended before the model was loaded

failures.description: Failed starts in a row with the same settings

settings_reverted.description: This failure made the server go back to the last good settings

exists.description: false for saved settings of a model that is not in the list

hidden.description: true for a model that `GET /v1/models` does not list but that is accepted when requested (such a row comes only from `?model=`; the list shows its saved settings under `unattached`, kind `hidden`)

overrides.description: Custom settings saved in the panel (canonical spelling)

kept.description: Values of the model's entry in `admin-models.json` that the server does not use (an unknown key or an invalid value, e.g. written by a newer version or by hand); written back unchanged

fields.description: Every whitelisted key with its effective value, origin and lock

phase.description: State of the saved settings: `pending` saved, not tried; `trial` a start with them is under way; `committed` the model reached loaded with them (they become `last_good`); `failed` the process ended before loaded. null = no custom settings

failures.description: Failed starts in a row with the current settings; at 2 the server reverts to `last_good`

last_good.description: The custom settings the model last reached loaded with

reverted.description: Set when the server replaced the settings with `last_good` (two failed starts in a row, or at start-up)

reverted_at_startup.description: The entry was still in `trial` / `failed` at start-up, so the model started with its last good settings

device_moved.description: The saved GPU name now belongs to a GPU with another PCI bus id than when it was saved; the value is still applied

now_named.description: The name the saved GPU has now, if it is still there

device_missing.description: The saved GPU is not on this server; the value is not applied and the model uses its inherited GPU

apply_error.description: Why saved values are not applied (e.g. a hand-edited file); empty when fine

context.description: What the context settings mean for one request, from the effective values

unified.description: One KV pool shared by all slots

pool.description: KV pool in tokens (ctx-size rounded up to 256)

max_per_request.description: min(pool or pool per slot, per-slot cap, trained context)

per_request_all_busy.description: Tokens per request when every slot is busy (about pool / slots)

facts_status.description: Model facts read from the GGUF file: `pending` = being read in the background

facts.description: Facts from the model file: `arch`, `n_layer`, `n_ctx_train`, `n_embd`, head counts and sizes, `quant`, `files`, the tensor sizes the rough estimate uses, `kv_bytes_per_token` per KV cache type (`f16`, `bf16`, `q8_0`, `q4_0`; null when the type is not possible for the model, e.g. `q8_0` / `q4_0` with a head size that is not a multiple of 32, or a recurrent / MLA model), `kv_estimate` (`exact`, `approximate`, `unsupported`) and `kv_note` (why). With `facts_status` `error`: `error`, e.g. `the GGUF metadata of ... is not plausible (...)`, a `split.count` that does not match the file name, or a missing part of a split model

warnings.description: Codes such as `model_devices_not_applied` (MODEL_DEVICES names the model but its section does not carry that device), `device_moved`, `device_missing`, `default_device_not_present`, `pool_overcommit`, `ctx_above_train`, `ubatch_above_ctx`, `kv_per_slot_no_effect`, `pooling_without_embeddings`, `apply_error`

schema.description: The whitelist with type, range, allowed values, built-in default and group of every key, for forms

default.description: Built-in default; null when the model decides (e.g. its trained context)

values.description: `enum`: the allowed values; `ngl`: the words allowed besides a number

auto.description: The number that means auto (`-1` for `parallel`)

pair.description: The key this one must be equal to (`cache-type-k` / `cache-type-v`)

build_devices.description: GPUs of this server; empty for a CPU-only build

unattached.description: Saved settings of models that are not in the list; kept until removed with `reset`

warnings.description: `default_device_not_present`, `model_devices_unknown_section:<name>` (a MODEL_DEVICES entry that names no models.ini section)

AdminUnattachedEntry.description: Saved settings of a model that is not in the list (also the answer of `GET /admin/models/settings?model=<id>` for such an id, then with `state`)

kind.description: `orphaned`: the model is gone (deleted, renamed); `hidden`: a cache entry the list does not show; `unreadable`: an entry of the file that could not be read (kept as it is, see `raw`)

raw.description: `unreadable` only: the entry as it is in the file

error.description: Why the file could not be read; empty when fine

read_only.description: true = the file is damaged or from a newer version; saving answers 409 `model_settings_read_only`

backup_loaded.description: The file could not be read and its `.bak` was used

problems.description: Entries or values that were skipped while reading

model.description: Model id, or the id of an entry in `unattached`

reset.description: Remove all custom settings of the model

restart.description: Running model: restart it with the new settings (without it the change is refused with 409). Stopped model: load it right away

changed.description: false = the effective values did not change; nothing was reloaded or restarted

restarted_also.description: Other models that were loaded before, went down when the model list was rebuilt, and were loaded again

not_restarted.description: Other models that went down and could not be loaded again

load_error.description: Saved, but the model could not be started now (e.g. `model limit reached`); it starts on its next request. Empty when fine

reload_error.description: Always empty in a 200 answer: a failed rebuild of the model list is a 500 (`error.reload_error`) and the previous settings are restored

AdminReloadError.description: The error answer of `POST /admin/models/settings` when the settings could not be applied

reload_error.description: Why the model list could not be rebuilt (missing when the settings file could not be written)

restarted.description: Only when the model was running and had been stopped for the restart: true = it runs again with its previous settings, false = see `restart_error`

restarted_also.description: Only when not empty: other models that were loaded before and were loaded again

not_restarted.description: Only when not empty: other models that were loaded before and could not be loaded again

ok.description: false = llama.cpp could not set the model up with these settings, see `error`

cached.description: The result of an earlier check: same model, effective arguments, GPU inventory and running state, at most 60 s old, and the live free memory of its GPUs moved by less than 256 MiB

checked_while_running.description: The dry run was made while the model was running: its fit saw the model's own memory as used (missing in an answer with `ok: false`)

verdict.description: The worst verdict of all devices (`no`, then `unknown`, then `tight`); `cpu_only`: the model uses no GPU (a CPU-only server, or `device` `none`), `devices` is empty and `host` has its memory

need.description: Bytes the model would need on this GPU

free.description: Free memory of the GPU now

own_usage.description: What the model uses there now, counted as available when it is running and would be restarted

settling.description: A model on this GPU is loading or stopping: verdict `unknown`

verdict.description: `fits`: need + margin <= available; `tight`: need <= available < need + margin; `no`: need > available; `unknown`: memory not known or settling

host.description: Host memory the model would need (model, context, compute)

args.description: The command line of the dry run (what the model process would get)

duration_ms.description: How long a new check took (not in a cached answer)

n_gpu_layers.description: The GPU layers llama.cpp's fit chose

fit.description: Result of llama.cpp's fit (`off`: the fit was switched off for this model)

line.description: The output line of llama.cpp the code comes from

AdminGpuInventory.description: The GPUs the inventory helper found (at start-up, or at the last `POST /admin/gpus/rescan`)

error.description: Why it failed (`timeout`, `failed`, `parse_error`, `unsupported`, `disabled`); the GPU names then come from the backends only

name.description: Device name as the backend registers it (CUDA0, ROCm0, Vulkan0, SYCL0, ...)

device_id.description: Device id as the backend reports it

pci_bus_id.description: PCI bus id, lower case `dddd:bb:dd.f`; null when the backend reports none

mapping.description: How the vendor tool's row was matched to this GPU

index.description: Index of the vendor tool's row (not the device number)

unsupported.description: The tool reports no usable memory for this GPU (e.g. MIG, vGPU)

memory_source.description: `inventory` = measured at start-up / last re-detect, see `memory_age_ms`

settling.description: A model on this GPU is loading or stopping (or did so a moment ago): the free memory is not final

same_gpu_as.description: Other device names of the same physical GPU (e.g. CUDA0 and Vulkan0)

all_gpus.description: The model has no GPU of its own and may use every GPU

source.description: `reported` by the model process itself (its memory breakdown, printed at log verbosity 4), `measured` per process by nvidia-smi (host only), or a rough `estimate`

by.description: `model` (reported), `nvidia-smi` (measured), `llama.cpp` (estimate from a fit check of the current settings) or `formula` (estimate from the model file)

gpu_backend.description: The GPU backends of this server

state.description: `cpu_only`: no GPU backend in this build; `no_devices`: a GPU backend is there but found no GPU (driver, permissions such as /dev/kfd or /dev/dri, container without GPUs)

libraries.description: GPU backend libraries next to the binary

message.description: The error in words, e.g. the tool's first error line

stale.description: The last run failed; the figures are from an older run

mapping.description: How the tool's rows were matched to the GPUs: by PCI bus id, the one GPU with the one row, not at all, a mix, or no GPU

id.description: `deployment`, `binary`, `gpu_backend`, `inventory`, `vendor_tool`, `memory_mapping`, `router_gpu_free`, `state_dir`, `admin_key`, `proxy`, `ip_allowlist`, `model_devices`, `model_settings`, and `stuck_helpers` at the end, only while a helper process hangs

value.description: What was found: a string, a number, a boolean, an object or null

hint.description: One line on what to do or what it means

AdminUploadAvailability.description: Whether GGUF files can be uploaded on this server

reason.description: null when available. `no_models_dir`: no `--models-dir` (Docker: mount `/models-rw`; host: add it to `PROVISION_LLM_ARGS`; then restart). `models_dir_missing`, `not_writable`: fix the directory. `staging_unusable`: `.provision-upload` in the models directory is a file or a symbolic link. `staging_other_filesystem`: something is mounted over `.provision-upload`

message.description: The reason in words, with what to do

chunk_default.description: Chunk size a client starts with

chunk_min.description: Smallest chunk a client steps down to when a proxy limits the request size

max_sessions.description: Unfinished uploads at the same time

max_writers.description: Chunks received at the same time over all uploads

ttl_h.description: Hours without progress after which an upload is removed (counted while the server runs)

max_header_bytes.description: Largest metadata section of a file

AdminUploadSummary.description: One upload in the list of `GET /admin/models/upload`

name.description: The model id it will get

blocked_by.description: `ready` only: what the upload waits for; details in `blocked`

durable_offset.description: Bytes known to be on disk (last checkpoint, every 256 MiB or 15 s); after a restart of the server `offset` goes back to it

role.description: From the header check; null before

record_persisted.description: The upload's record is in the admin state directory

checks.description: What the checks found so far (the header check names architecture, parameters, quantization, training context)

last_modified.description: Milliseconds since the epoch; a hint for matching the file after a reload

sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 (as Hugging Face shows it)

settings_mode.description: Saved settings of an earlier model with this id: `replace` drops them, `keep` uses them again with `settings` on top

upload.description: The new upload, as `GET /admin/models/upload?id=` shows it; in a dry run only `id` (null), `name`, `files`, `settings`, `chunk_max`, `chunk_default`

disk.description: The filesystem of the models directory

other_uploads_bytes.description: What the other unfinished uploads still need

shares_disk_with.description: Other data on the same filesystem: `admin_state`

existing_settings.description: Only when there are some: saved settings of an earlier model with this id (an `orphaned` entry of `GET /admin/models/settings`)

offset.description: The file's offset on the server after this chunk

state.description: The upload's state; `checking` once every file is complete

file_error.description: Why this file cannot be used, once the header check decided so

files.description: Set the expected SHA-256 of files (an empty string removes it)

drop_files.description: Indexes of files to take out of the upload; their data is deleted at once

ignore_sha256_mismatch.description: Publish although the SHA-256 differs from the expected one

without_settings.description: Publish without the upload's settings (when they cannot be saved: `settings_not_saved`)

AdminUploadAnswer.description: Answer of update, publish and cancel

dry_run.description: Only report what would be deleted

stop.description: Stop the model first if it is running (otherwise 409 `model_running`)

remove_settings.description: Also remove its saved per-model settings, its pin and what the server cached about it

projector_only.description: Remove projector: delete only the model's projector file

files.description: What is (would be) deleted, paths relative to the models directory

kept.description: Other entries of the model's folder that stay (not part of this model); at most 100 listed

folder.description: The model's folder in the models directory; null for a top-level file

folder_removed.description: The folder is (would be) empty afterwards and removed

running.description: Dry run: the model is running (it would be stopped with `stop`)

has_settings.description: Dry run: the model has saved per-model settings

warnings.description: Dry run: `running`, `folder_keeps_other_model` (another GGUF file stays in the folder and may be listed under this id afterwards)

trash_left.description: The files wait in the trash, which the server deletes in the background

reload_error.description: The model list could not be rebuilt afterwards; the files are gone all the same

param.description: Admin validation and lock errors: the request field the error is about, a key of `settings` (e.g. `ctx-size`), `settings` or `model`

license.description: Present on 403 responses from the license gate

max_tokens.description: OpenAI name; native alias is n_predict

input.description: A string, or a list of input items
A string or array of strings to embed

query.example: What is the capital of France?

documents.description: Candidate documents to score against the query

top_n.description: Return only the top N results

index.description: Index into the input documents array

prompt.description: Optional extra prompt inserted between prefix and suffix
